trajectory_messages.content:
Implement chunk-level health tracking in the container Merkle tree system of Apache Ozone. Extend the functionality to include a health flag for chunks, support incremental updates from serialized trees, and register an on-demand scanner callback.

*   Modify `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter`:
    *   Update `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo> chunks)` to include a `boolean healthy` parameter. Ensure each `ChunkMerkleTree` entry has `isHealthy` set according to this parameter.
    *   Add a varargs overload `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ContainerProtos.ChunkInfo... chunks)` to accept multiple `ChunkInfo` instances directly.
    *   Introduce `addBlock(long blockID)` to insert an empty block into the tree without affecting existing entries.
    *   Implement a new constructor `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)` that initializes the writer from an existing proto. Ensure `toProto()` outputs identical to the input proto, including empty blocks.
    *   Ensure the writer remains mutable after initialization from a proto, allowing further updates with `addChunks` or `addBlock`.

*   Update the `ChunkMerkleTree` protobuf message:
    *   Add a `boolean isHealthy` field.
    *   Provide access via `getIsHealthy()` and `setIsHealthy(boolean)` methods.

*   Rename method in `KeyValueHandler`:
    *   Change `createContainerMerkleTree` to `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` to clarify it reads from metadata.
    *   Update all internal call sites to use the new method name.

*   Enhance `ContainerSet`:
    *   Add `registerContainerScanHandler(Function<Container, Optional<Future<?>>> scanHandler)` to allow registration of an on-demand scan handler.
    *   Ensure the handler is invoked automatically during reconciliation to trigger container scans.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.

BUILD SUCCESS — the `container-service` module (which contains all four modified classes plus `OzoneContainer`) compiles cleanly.

## Summary

All changes are in source files only; no test files were touched. The protobuf `ChunkMerkleTree.isHealthy` field already existed in the repo, so `getIsHealthy()`/`setIsHealthy()` are available as generated accessors.

**`ContainerMerkleTreeWriter.java`**
- `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, Collection<ChunkInfo>)` — added the `healthy` param; each `ChunkMerkleTree` entry now gets `isHealthy` set from it (via `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter(chunk, healthy)`).
- `addChunks(long blockID, boolean healthy, ChunkInfo... chunks)` — new varargs overload delegating to the collection form.
- `addBlock(long blockID)` — inserts an empty block via `computeIfAbsent` without disturbing existing entries.
- `ContainerMerkleTreeWriter(ContainerProtos.ContainerMerkleTree fromTree)` — new constructor rebuilding the writer from a proto. Added `BlockMerkleTreeWriter.addChunkTrees(...)` and a `ChunkMerkleTreeWriter(ChunkMerkleTree)` constructor that preserve stored offset/length/isHealthy/dataChecksum instead of recomputing, so `toProto()` reproduces the input exactly (including empty blocks, which are preserved by `computeIfAbsent`). The writer stays mutable — further `addChunks`/`addBlock` calls work after init.

**`KeyValueHandler.java`**
- Renamed `createContainerMerkleTree` → `createContainerMerkleTreeFromMetadata` and updated all 4 internal call sites.
- Updated the `updateAndGetContainerChecksum` call site to the new `addChunks(id, true, chunkInfos)` signature.

**`ContainerSet.java`**
- `registerContainerScanHandler` now takes `Function<Container<?>, Optional<Future<?>>>` (field type updated to match). `scanContainer` invokes it via `apply(...)`, and reconciliation (`KeyValueHandler.reconcileContainer`) already calls `containerSet.scanContainer(...)`, so the handler fires automatically during reconciliation. The existing `OzoneContainer` registration (`onDemandScanner::scanContainer`, which returns `Optional<Future<?>>`) remains compatible.

One note: I kept the `registerContainerScanHandler` parameter typed as `Function<Container<?>, Optional<Future<?>>>` (with the `<?>`) rather than the raw `Container` shown in the spec — this matches the existing `OnDemandContainerDataScanner.scanContainer(Container<?>)` method reference cleanly and avoids raw-type warnings while being functionally identical for lambda/method-ref callers.
